Tucson, Arizona · ride

Bike routes in Tucson

The rides locals in Tucson actually do, each with a public route page you can load on your computer. Real miles, real feet, where it starts, where the water is, and the line about what will get you hurt.

Best months: October to April, when the roads are dry and the days are mild. Summer highs run near 100 F from June through August. In summer Pima County says to ride the Loop before 9 a.m. or after 5 p.m. The top of Mount Lemmon runs 20 to 30 F colder than town, with ice in the shade from December to February. Winter storms close the road.

Bike routes in Tucson, listed

  1. Mount Lemmon (the Catalina Highway)

    Climb · 28 mi · 6,770 ft · epic · Paved. Smooth to about mile 21, then more cracks and bumps; the first three miles were repaved in 2024.

    RideWithGPSRoute page

    The climb from the desert floor at mile marker 0 (2,858 feet) to the observatory at the top: 27.8 miles and about 6,770 feet of climbing (Bike Mount Lemmon), the road GABA’s Mt. Lemmon Hill Climb climbs (on the 2027 calendar for May 7, projected). The main climb averages 4.7 percent; the last stretch to the observatory is close to 7. Windy Point is at mile 14. At the top, in Summerhaven, Bike Mount Lemmon lists the Mt. Lemmon Cookie Cabin, the general store and Sawmill Run for food. The Cookie Cabin’s own page says to check Google Maps for closures before you count on it. If you drive to the bottom, Bike Mount Lemmon points you to the LeBuzz Caffe and Safeway lot at Tanque Verde Road and the Catalina Highway, 4.5 miles from mile 0. LeBuzz opens at 6, and Earlybird Bikes, which rents road bikes, is on the same road. A RideWithGPS version from town is 59.3 miles and 6,866 feet round trip.

    Start: Mile marker 0, Catalina Highway, 5315 Mt Lemmon Hwy, Tucson, AZ 85749

    Water: None on the climb until the Bigelow trailhead, past mile marker 19 (Bike Mount Lemmon; the University of Arizona cycling team says mile 19.5). Windy Point, at mile 14, has pit toilets and no water. Before the climb, McDonald Park off Harrison Road is a short detour for water (UA cycling).

    Watch: The top runs 20 to 30 F colder than the bottom, and gusts over 30 mph come up, mostly in the afternoon. Ice forms in the shade from December to February. Going down, the shoulder is narrower than on the way up, and cars move into it on the curves. Winter weather closes the road: in January 2026 it reopened at noon on Jan 8 to four-wheel-drive, all-wheel-drive or chained vehicles only (KOLD, from the Pima County Sheriff). Pima County’s roads hotline is 520-351-3351.

  2. The Loop (Chuck Huckelberry Loop)

    Path · 54 mi · easy · Paved shared-use path, with short stretches of buffered bike lane.

    Route page

    Any length you want. Pima County’s car-free path along the Santa Cruz River, the Rillito, the Pantano Wash, Julian Wash, the Harrison Road Greenway and the Cañada del Oro. The full circuit is 53.9 miles; the whole system is more than 138 miles and reaches Marana and Oro Valley. You can join it anywhere and turn around anywhere, so it is the ride for the evening you land. The University of Arizona cycling team calls it fantastic for easy spins, with the quieter east and south sections good for tempo. From downtown, join it where Congress Street crosses the river. The Mercado San Agustín, with Presta’s coffee, Seis Kitchen and Transit Cycles, is less than half a mile away, and The Tuxon is two blocks off the path. GABA’s social ride (Some Tuesdays, 7:00 am) rides much of it; the Heirloom market at Rillito Park sits right on the Rillito stretch.

    Start: Where Congress Street crosses the Loop on the Santa Cruz River, west of downtown

    Water: Most trailheads have water fountains and restrooms (Visit Tucson).

    Watch: Open sunrise to sunset; riding it at night is prohibited. In summer, Pima County says carry enough water and ride before 9 a.m. or after 5 p.m. Julian Wash from Kino to Irvington is closed indefinitely while the Mosaic Quarter sports complex is built; the county posts a paved detour along I-10. Storms leave sand in the underpasses: the Julian Wash underpass at Benson Highway closed for it in August 2026. Check Pima County’s Loop closures page before a long day.

  3. The Shootout

    Road · 70 mi · 1,600 ft · hard · Paved road.

    RideWithGPSRoute page

    The Shootout (Saturdays, 7:00 am) is Tucson’s fast group ride. The groups leave University and Euclid by pace and head south through the San Xavier Mission district, left at Nogales Highway and Sahuarita Road by Helmet Peak, over to Mission Road and back into town on it. Fair Wheel Bikes, which posts the start times and sits nearby on 6th Street, puts it at about 70 miles for the A group (22 to 28+ mph) and the Scootout (19 to 23). The Old-Old Man group (16 to 20) rides a shorter day. A RideWithGPS version from the university is 59.9 miles and 1,595 feet. Ride it alone any day, or start with the slowest group. Time Market on University Boulevard opens at 7 for the coffee after.

    Start: University Blvd & Euclid Ave, by the University of Arizona

    Watch: Self-supported: Fair Wheel says bring water, food and flat repair, and know the route before you go. It has a mid-ride stop. To Be Determined’s guide says it’s casual until Mission Road crosses Valencia, then race pace. The A group is for racers.

    Ride it with the group: The Shootout (Saturdays, 7:00 am) →

  4. Gates Pass and the McCain Loop

    Road · 18 mi · 1,500 ft · moderate · Paved road; rough pavement on Kinney Road.

    RideWithGPS

    Over Gates Pass in the Tucson Mountains west of town and around the McCain Loop: 17.9 miles and about 1,500 feet, per the RideWithGPS page. Gates Pass is the main climb on the University of Arizona cycling team’s Tuesday route, and the team says the pass is a great ride on its own. A longer RideWithGPS version is 38.7 miles and 2,244 feet, with a food stop at El Guero Canelo near the end. The route pages give the numbers, not the start; read the map before you go. The Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, on Kinney Road, is the west side’s afternoon off the bike.

    Watch: No bike lanes on Gates Pass. Kinney Road has no bike lanes and rough pavement (University of Arizona cycling team, 2020).

  5. Cactus Forest Loop Drive (Saguaro National Park East)

    Road · 8 mi · easy · Paved, except the gravel spur to the Mica View picnic area.

    RideWithGPSRoute page

    An 8-mile paved loop through the saguaro forest in the park’s east district, per the park service. To Be Determined’s Tucson guide calls it mostly rolling, with one 650-foot climb. A rider pays $15 for a 7-day pass; under 16 is free (NPS, Oct 2026). A RideWithGPS version from a hotel in town is 28.5 miles and 1,264 feet. Cactus Cycling Club’s Saguaro East ride (Fridays, 7:30 am) loops the east side of the park and stops at LeBuzz after. El Tour’s course runs Old Spanish Trail past the park.

    Start: Saguaro National Park, Rincon Mountain District Visitor Center, 3693 S Old Spanish Trail, Tucson, AZ 85730

    Water: Outside the visitor center. None on the loop drive or at the picnic areas (NPS).

    Watch: The park service says the loop is narrow, with tight turns and steep hills, and to slow down before the curves and the hills.

  6. El Tour de Tucson century course

    Road · 102 mi · 3,000 ft · epic · Paved road.

    RideWithGPSRoute page

    The 102-mile course of El Tour de Tucson, the city’s biggest ride, ridden the Saturday before Thanksgiving (Nov 20, 2027, projected). It starts and finishes at the Tucson Convention Center at the south end of downtown. The organizer lists Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, Old Spanish Trail, Colossal Cave, Corona de Tucson, Vail, Sahuarita and Green Valley along the way. The organizer’s 2025 route on RideWithGPS is 101.7 miles and 3,007 feet. On event day the century starts at 7 a.m. and the routes close at 4:30 p.m.; the 62- and 32-mile courses start later. GABA runs El Tour training rides (Sundays, 6:45 am) in the weeks before the race, and the DoubleTree next to the convention center is the bed closest to the start.

    Start: Tucson Convention Center

    Water: On event day, aid stations about every 12 miles (organizer). Nothing published for riding it on another day.

    Watch: On any other day the roads are open to traffic, and the course runs through Davis-Monthan Air Force Base; check whether you can get through the base before you ride it on your own.

  7. Sweetwater Preserve trails

    Mountain bike · 8 mi · 500 ft · moderate · Singletrack.

    Route page

    The most-ridden loop of the Sweetwater trail system, about 7 miles northwest of downtown: Saguaro Vista, Sun Circle, Black Rock, Lost Arrow, Red Canyon and Red Tail Ridge, then Wildflower Ridge back to the trailhead. 7.7 miles and 479 feet, per MTB Project, which calls it mostly easy with a few intermediate sections. Lost Arrow is a sustained climb that’s a stretch for a beginner. Dogs on leash; MTB Project lists e-bikes as not allowed. Sonoran Desert Mountain Bicyclists, the trail club, runs fall trail-work days here.

    Start: Sweetwater Preserve trailhead

    Watch: Shared with hikers and horses (MTB Project).
